body:
Crypto markets continued their brutal selloff today with the total market cap shedding another 2.59% to $2.18 trillion as extreme fear gripped traders for the second consecutive day. The Fear & Greed index remained pinned at 12, reflecting the panic that has wiped over $200 billion from Bitcoin's market cap alone in recent sessions. Volume surged to $164.5 billion as liquidations mounted, with $1.6 billion in positions getting crushed over the past 24 hours. Bitcoin dominance held steady at 56.1% while traders fled risk assets across the board, though the selling pressure showed signs of exhaustion in the final hours.

Bitcoin found some footing above $61,000 after yesterday's savage drop below $60,000 triggered mass liquidations, closing at $61,134 down 2.94% on the day despite the late bounce. The 7-day decline now stands at a brutal 16.73% with $67.22 billion in volume reflecting the heavy institutional repositioning. Key support at $58,000 held firm during the worst of the selling, while resistance now sits at $65,000. The funding rate collapse has bears positioned for potential pain if this oversold bounce gains momentum, with some analysts eyeing a short squeeze scenario given the extreme negative sentiment.

Ethereum got hammered worse than Bitcoin, plunging 6.11% to $1,578.84 and hitting 13-month lows as the Zcash bug news sparked broader smart contract concerns. The 7-day drop of 21.52% has ETH dominance sliding to just 8.7% as altcoins face systematic derisking. Solana led the carnage among major alts with a 4.43% decline to $63.18, extending its weekly loss to 23.11%. Cardano social activity paradoxically surged as ADA crashed under $0.16 to 4-year lows, down 32.16% over 7 days. The relative outperformance came from BNB at just 2.05% down, benefiting from Binance's operational resilience narrative.

The macro backdrop remains toxic with AI security vulnerabilities exposing flaws in major crypto networks just as regulatory scrutiny intensifies ahead of Tuesday's House tax hearing. Geopolitical tensions continue weighing on risk assets while the Fed's hawkish stance keeps traditional safe havens attractive relative to crypto's volatility. Arthur Hayes' WorldCoin dump after publicly stating he'd hold added to the sentiment damage, highlighting how quickly narratives can shift in this environment. The combination of technical failures, regulatory uncertainty, and macro headwinds has created a perfect storm for crypto bears.

All eyes now turn to whether Bitcoin can hold $58,000 support and spark the short squeeze that funding data suggests is brewing. Tuesday's crypto tax hearing could provide the next major catalyst, with any hawkish regulatory signals likely to extend the selloff. Conversely, signs of institutional buying at these oversold levels or positive regulatory developments could trigger violent short covering given the extreme positioning. The $65,000 level on Bitcoin remains the key reclaim target that would signal the bleeding has stopped, while a break below $58,000 opens the door to a retest of 2023 lows.
